messages:
sarah: Heads-up — a SOC customer reported that exported audit rows for policy changes show actor_id only (e.g. user_843) when the account was later deleted. They need a stable, human-readable 'who' column in CSV/NDJSON for compliance reporting.

mike: Is the display name not stored on the event at write-time? I thought our change events already include actor_name.

jordan: We currently store actor_id + a small actor_snapshot for some event types, but retention TTL prunes snapshots aggressively for writes older than 90d. Exports go back years, so older rows lose readable names.

eli: Right. Options: 1) keep actor_snapshot indefinitely (cost), 2) expand export to join actor table at export-time (fast but breaks if actor deleted), 3) add a human-readable audit_alias field at write time that persists.

katie: GDPR note: if a user exercises right-to-be-forgotten, we can't keep plain PII forever. We need a pseudonymization plan (e.g., keep a hashed display + non-reversible tag).

mike: Proposed hybrid: write actor_display for events but support a "redact_on_erasure" flag. If customer requests erasure, we replace actor_display with "redacted" and keep an opaque actor_fingerprint for internal correlation.

jordan: Implementation constraints: writes are ~10k/sec. Adding a string field to each event is cheap from a write path perspective (few bytes) but increases storage by ~15-30% depending on avg name length. Exports size also grows. Need cost calc.

eli: For exports UX, we can introduce an export param expand_actor=true that attempts to resolve latest identities at export time and a snapshot_name field that is the original name. For deleted users, expand_actor would return "Deleted user (uid=user_843)".

sarah: Customer asks for "who changed X" in a single CSV column without manually joining. They also want the reason text and IP if available. Can we include a minimal set by default?

katie: Default should be privacy-safe: include snapshot_name (pseudonymized) + role_at_time + action. Admins with proper access can request full export (include email/ip) behind an endpoint that records justification.

mike: Rollout idea: 1) start writing snapshot_name to new events (no backfill). 2) add export-time join that prefers snapshot_name then falls back to actor table if allowed. 3) provide migration job to backfill snapshot_name for historical events for customers who opt in.

jordan: Backfill cost: scanning ~2B events. We could do customer-scoped backfills on demand via long-running job. Need quota/billing for backfill.

eli: Telemetry: add metrics for export-time expand_hits, expand_misses, and redaction_hits so we can see impact. Also track storage delta per customer label to bill if they keep snapshot retention beyond default.

katie: Compliance: add a documented data retention policy per workspace and an API to request redaction for events. Must include audit trail of the redaction request itself (who requested, when, justification). That redaction record should be exportable.

sarah: UI copy: in audit viewer show name precedence: snapshot_name (bold) -> resolved_current_name (faded) -> "Deleted user". Hover shows provenance: "snapshot written at 2025-11-01T12:23Z".

mike: Edge case: service accounts and integrations change keys; we should store actor_kind (human|service|integration) and include it in exports.

eli: Security: storing snapshot_name could be flagged by InfoSec. We'll add encryption-at-rest + KMS key per-customer for Private deployments. For Hosted, store pseudonymous snapshot by default; allow plaintext snapshot only with opt-in and legal review.

jordan: API shape proposal for NDJSON export: each line has: event_id, ts, action, actor_id, actor_kind, snapshot_name, snapshot_name_pseudonym (bool), reason, ip, meta. We'll default to omitting ip unless requester has audit:read:full scope.

sarah: Sample export param: ?since=2024-01-01&expand_actor=false&include_ip=false&format=ndjson. Mentioned backfill opt-in as separate endpoint POST /v1/audit/backfill?workspace=xyz.

katie: Legal ask: ensure we can redact snapshot_name on erasure and still preserve non-identifying event data. Add redact API: POST /v1/audit/redact { event_ids: [...], requester: ... }. The redaction itself gets an audit event.

mike: Dev plan: P0: write snapshot_name for new events + add actor_kind + telemetry. P1: export param + UI precedence + redaction API. P2: on-demand backfill + billing for backfill. P3: encrypted snapshots per-customer.

eli: Can we do a little experiment: add snapshot_name to the change_event table for one shard and run sample exports to measure size/CPU? If perf hit <5% we roll.

jordan: I'll spin up a canary and run a 7-day simulated export. Need test customers and a feature flag.

sarah: Action items: Jordan -> canary + perf test (ETA 3 days). Mike -> draft NDJSON schema + export params (ETA 2 days). Katie -> compliance writeup and redaction API sketch (ETA 4 days). Eli -> telemetry events list and KMS requirements (ETA 3 days). I'll sync with @legal after writeups.

audit-bot: Job 834 scheduled: canary export run queued by @jordan.

mike: One more: add a small notice in Console export flow: "Export may contain pseudonymized identifiers if user data was erased. Contact support for full context."

katie: +1. Also include retention settings in workspace settings with knob: "Keep identity snapshots for N days (default 90)" and explain cost/impact.

sarah: Thanks all — this feels like a solid path forward. We'll capture design in the eng RFC and link to the ticket.

mike: thanks — throwing the NDJSON schema in #eng-platform RFC channel when ready.

jordan: canary started. will post results in this thread.

audit-bot: Job 834 completed: export sample (10k events) size delta +18% snapshot_name present for 100% of new events. Performance impact: 1.8% CPU increase.
